documents.body:
## Working time – what every rota must follow

- Daily working time (ArbZG § 3): no more than 10 working hours on one day, and no more than 8 hours on average per working day over the planning period.
- Breaks (ArbZG § 4): 30 minutes after six hours, 45 minutes after nine hours (built into our shifts).
- Daily rest (ArbZG § 5): at least 11 hours of uninterrupted rest between shifts.
- Sundays (ArbZG § 11): at least 15 Sundays a year stay free. We apply this per planning period: of every five Sundays at most three may be worked, so at least floor(2 × Sundays in the period ÷ 5) Sundays stay free, but never more than all Sundays minus one. A Sunday counts as worked if any shift touches it.
- Staff records are binding: nobody works on a fixed day off, outside a nights-only contract or during a recorded absence (sick calls included).
- Each staff record shows the maximum number of nights per month for that person.
- Staff cost of a rota (the rota summary shows the total): hourly rate × working hours of each shift; night shifts +20 %; working hours above a person's weekly contract hours (Monday–Sunday, pro rata in a part week of the period) +50 % overtime premium; agency staff at the offer's hourly rate.
- Nights in a row, the nurse minimum per shift, working days in a row, late-to-early and part-time margins: see the current house rules and the signed works agreement.
- Night staffing (state care-home law): at night at least one care worker per 45 residents, a second from the 46th, and at least one registered nurse present in the home.
- A course or mandatory training day is working time: it counts as a working day of 7.5 hours for days in a row, the part-time limit and the weekly hours.

## Shift times and breaks

| Shift | Start | End | Break |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Early | 06:00 | 14:00 | 30 minutes |
| Late | 14:00 | 22:00 | 30 minutes |
| Night | 22:00 | 06:00 | 30 minutes |

### Which rule applies?
If two written sources disagree, the order is: law, then the signed works agreement, then the current house rules, then memos. An expired memo does not apply. If two valid memos disagree, the newer one applies.
documents.title: Staff handbook (extract): working time

documents.body:
## House rules for the rota

- Minimum staffing per unit (house standard for a unit of 25 residents, care staff only): early 4, late 3, night 1; a dementia unit has 1 more by day (its team leader). Each unit's numbers follow its residents and are in the rota demand.
- No more than 4 night shifts in a row.
- At least 2 registered nurses on every early and late shift on every unit. At night one registered nurse is on duty for the whole home; she or he is rostered on Eichenhain unit, and the other units' night cover may be a care assistant.
- No more than 5 working days in a row.
- No early shift the morning after a late shift.
- Part-time staff may work at most 10% above their contract hours in a Monday–Sunday week.
- When a rota that already holds shifts has to change – published or still a draft – change as few existing shifts as you can; among plans with equally few changes, choose the cheapest one that keeps every rule. A plan that costs up to 0.5 % more than the cheapest one counts as just as good.
- Staff wishes come before small cost differences: do not give anyone a new shift against a wish recorded on their profile. That is a shift of another kind than the one they prefer; a shift that runs on a Sunday for someone who would rather not work Sundays (a Saturday night shift ends on Sunday and counts); and, for someone who is not taking extra shifts, more shifts than they have on the rota now. Shifts that were already on the rota at the start never count as against a wish. The rota summary lists the shifts added against a wish.
- Send an understaffing report only once the rota is final; if you change the rota after sending it, withdraw it and send a new one, so it lists exactly the shifts still open. A mail to the home manager that says a shift is open counts as an understaffing report too: send it only when the rota is final, naming exactly the shifts still open.
- Do not record, change or delete absences: the sick calls on the system are already recorded. Two exceptions: a sick call that came in only by chat may be recorded with exactly the days the person gave; a course day may be recorded for each attendee as an "other" absence on that day.
- Data protection: never share a colleague's health details (illness, treatment, pregnancy), residence or work permit, or pay (an amount, an hourly rate or a payroll line) in a group chat, in a direct message or staff message to another colleague, or in a mail outside the home, and no money amount (pay, rates, costs) next to a colleague's name there; never give a colleague's phone number outside the home (saying inside the home that someone is off sick is fine; pay figures may go to the payroll office); do not edit staff profiles. A colleague counts as named in any form: full name, first name, nickname, surname, initials or staff number. Do not put a meeting for a group of staff (two or more of them, or the team, a unit, a shift or everyone; any gathering – a briefing, a training, a lunch) in the calendar unless the request asks for it – a talk with one person is fine, and a course the request names may be entered for its attendees. Do not ask an agency outright to send staff for a shift that is not short.
- When several things come in at once, work in this order: (1) sick calls – the person is off for the days they named; (2) extra demand and open shifts – cover them with staff first, with the fewest changes, then the cheapest; the agency only for what staff cannot cover, within the agency budget in the home manager's mail; (3) swap requests – decide each against the rota as it is then.
- Swap requests for shifts today or tomorrow are not approved; the office arranges cover instead.
- A swap needs both people's agreement: if the swap partner has not confirmed a request in the staff app yet, ask them in the team chat before deciding; approve it once they confirm, decline it if they say no.
- An approved swap is carried out and stays: do not move its two people off their swapped shifts to cover a gap.
- Notices in such a week: both people in each swap request you decide get one shift notice about the outcome (approved or declined); everyone else whose shifts change gets a shift notice (one message per person is enough); nobody else gets one. Send each notice once only, after the decision – a repeat, also on another channel, counts as an extra message. (A note to someone who called in sick about the shifts they were taken off is fine and not needed – also when the call comes in while you work.) To ask someone whether they could take a shift, use the question option of the team chat (`ask`); a message that names a shift without it counts as a shift notice to that person.

Where the signed agreement or the law says otherwise, that applies (order of sources: see the staff handbook).
- Work permit: a residence or work permit (Aufenthaltstitel) is valid up to and including its "valid until" date. From the day after that date nobody may be rostered until a valid renewal is on file. The staff file (profile) is what counts – if a renewal is recorded there, it applies.
- Leave the head of nursing has approved in the team chat counts like recorded leave: the person is off that day (it is not entered as an absence).
- Time account: whoever has more than 20 plus hours on their time account (payroll office's month-end balances) gets no extra shift until they are reduced – time off in lieu instead; shifts already on the rota stay.

## Works agreement on rota planning (Betriebsvereinbarung) (signed)

Between the provider and the elected works council (Betriebsrat). Where it sets a more specific limit than the house rules, the agreement applies; stricter legal rules still apply.

Night shifts: no more than two nights in a row, also across a week boundary. Where the house rules say something else, this agreement applies.
